The Project will also include over 7,000 SF of amenity spaces, 158 parking spaces, and 158 long-term bicycle parking spaces.  The Project also proposes significant site and public realm improvements that include reducing the amount of impervious surfaces, expanding the existing tree canopy, increasing the landscaping throughout the property, and encouraging multimodal transportation through the provision of a new blue-bike station and MBTA bus shelter.

Boston.name: 250 Everett Street
Boston.description: Mill Creek proposes to demolish the existing building and construct a new 6-story multifamily rental building of approximately 250,000 square feet, containing approximately 235 residential units and approximately 117 parking spaces in an underground parking structure.

Boston.name: 27 Farragut Road
Boston.description: The Proponent is proposing to construct a new four (4) story, twenty-one (21) unit residential rental building with garage parking for twenty-one (21) vehicles at 27 Farragut Road in South Boston.

Boston.name: New Madinah
Boston.description: The proposed project would raze the existing structure and surface parking to allow for the complete redevelopment of the site. As a mixed-use development, the project proposes 14,000 sf of cultural, commercial, and community services space, along with 38 new low-income tax credit units of housing (DND and DHCD compliant) and common roof deck and green roof, totaling approximately 34,236 sf. The project includes 4 surface parking spaces and 68 bike spaces (12 civic, 38 residential, and 81 public hitch).

Boston.name: Faneuil Gardens Phase 1
Boston.description: Faneuil Gardens is a redevelopment of an existing public housing community. Along with replacement units for all current public housing apartments, the intent is to add new income-restricted units, resident amenity space, and potential commercial/cultural spaces.

Boston.name: 88 Geneva Avenue
Boston.description: 39 homeownership units, with 24 parking spaces and 42 bicycle spaces, with a retail coffee shop.

Boston.name: 36 Parker Hill Avenue
Boston.description: The Rise at Longwood Development team is proposing a five (5) story building of approximately 30,861 square feet of gross floor area (“GFA”), including thirty-eight (38) residential rental apartments, with a mix of studios and two-bedrooms unit types. The ground floor programming accommodates a shared outdoor courtyard with new catenary exterior lighting, soft seating and pavers, a fitness/yoga studio, indoor/outdoor bike storage and a modest amount of off-street parking. The project also envisions an outdoor roof deck amenity for residents.

Boston.name: 615 Albany Street
Boston.description: The proposed project at 615 Albany is part of the Office to Residential Conversion Program. 615 Albany Street LCC (the proponent) is proposing the conversion of the existing 5 story, 19,200 square foot underutilized office space to residential use. Creating a 6 story ~20,000 square foot residential building with 24 units. Including: 12 studios, 1 1-bedroom, 6 2-bedrooms, and 5 3-bedrooms. 17% of the units will be IDP units and 3% held for voucher holders as per the Office to Residential Conversion Program standards.

Boston.name: 691-695 Morton Street
Boston.description: A six (6) story, twenty-nine (29) unit mixed-use building with a common roof deck and five (5) parking spaces, thirty-six (36) bicycle parking spaces, and retail space on the ground level.

Boston.name: 539-551 Centre Street
Boston.description: The Jamaica Plain Company, represented by Paul B. Clayton, proposes renovation of the existing multi-family residential Forbes Building in Jamaica Plain, constructed in 1978 on a 1.59-acre lot, with approximately 125,000 gsf of floor area, and which includes 147 multi-family units (130 one-bedroom and 17 two-bedrooms), 4,500 gsf of commercial space, and outdoor surface parking for 32 vehicles. The proposed affordability percentage in the Forbes Building is expected to be 97% (143 of 147 units). The new income averaging allows for LIHTC units to be up to 80% AMI as long as the average income of the tenants is at 60% AMI or lower. Most of the 143 LIHTC units will be at 60% AMI, with approximately 20 units up to 80% AMI. The Proponent is working with EOHLC to formulate a plan to add MRVP certificates over time that would allow the Forbes Building to serve lower-income tenants.

Boston.name: 50 Sutherland Road
Boston.description: The Developer plans to add 16 assisted living units to the existing building, renovate the first-floor dining and reception area and add outdoor decks.

Boston.name: 555-559 Columbia Road
Boston.description: The project proposes a five-story mixed-use structure with the bottom two floors occupied by the Boston Public Library and the upper three floors containing 33 workforce residential homeownership units. The project would have on-site parking in the basement.

Boston.name: 555 Talbot Avenue
Boston.description: Erect a new six-story mixed-use building to contain approximately 34 dwelling unit and a ground-floor restaurant, with no on-site parking.

Boston.name: 344-350 Washington Street
Boston.description: The Proposed Project involves the demolition of the existing structure on a 6,450 square foot lot to allow for the construction of a new (6) six-story, mixed-use building. The building will include approximately 1,007 square feet of ground-floor retail space, nineteen (19) condominium units, and seventeen (17) off-street parking spaces. In total, the new structure will encompass roughly 27,969 square feet and will provide twenty (20) residential bicycle parking spaces, along with six (6) additional bike spaces designated for visitors.

Boston.name: 81 Hancock Street
Boston.description: A four (4) story, thirty-six (36) unit mixed-use building with fifteen (15) parking spaces. The ground floor will offer a residential lobby and retail space for a liquor store and laundromat accessible to the public.

Boston.name: 2 Hillsboro Street
Boston.description: 21-unit new construction condominium project.  All units will be income-restricted, 18 units will have a preference for certified artists.

Boston.name: 141 Addison Street
Boston.description: The proposed project consists of a new four-story residential building situated at 141 Addison Street in East Boston’s Harborview Neighborhood. The project site is an 11,000-square-foot parcel currently occupied by a one-story commercial building with surface parking. The applicant proposes a new residential use with a twenty (20) unit residential building, with fourteen (14) accessory garage parking spaces and bicycle storage in accordance with Boston Transportation Department policy requirements.  The Proposed Project would redevelop an underutilized industrial site into residential development combining market-rate and affordable housing opportunities in an aesthetic appropriate in scale, massing, and design to this particular Neighborhood of East Boston, providing additional high-density housing for the area.

Boston.name: 157 Humboldt Avenue
Boston.description: Nehemiah Development is a joint venture between the Pleasant Hill Baptist Church (PHBC) and Nuestra Comunidad Development Corporation (NCDC). This new construction project will create 26 units of much needed family rental housing that will remain 100% affordable in perpetuity. This development will revitalize the neighborhood, located on the Dorchester/Roxbury line as it entails the demolition of a blighted vacant building and adjacent lot with sustainable and energy efficient family housing. The project will additionally offer 2,000 square feet of vibrant community space for the future residents and community as a central place for resources and gathering. The proposed project will occupy two adjacent lots owned by Pleasant Hill Baptist Church. These lots include a vacant structure at 157 Humboldt Avenue. This structure has been unused for over three decades. The second lot is vacant land located at 64 Waumbeck Street. The project site sits across the street from an active playground and is north of Boston’s Franklin Park. The design consists of a 4-story L-shaped building that will hold seven (7) one-bedroom units, fifteen (15) two-bedroom units, and four (4) three-bedroom units. The building will also feature high performance sustainable design that exceeds the City of Boston’s Net Zero Energy guidelines. The project will incorporate sustainable and energy-efficient design principles featuring passive house design, LEED Gold certification, and solar panels to minimize environmental impact and reduce ongoing costs for residents.

Boston.name: 470 Western Avenue
Boston.description: The project proposes the construction of a new six (6) story 39 unit residential building of approximately 34,647 square feet of gross floor area, with on-site parking for 14 vehicles, bicycle parking spaces and improvements in landscaping, pedestrian connectivity, and related public realm improvements in and around the Site, consistent with the character and housing needs of the surrounding community (the “Proposed Project”). The project is anticipated to include two (2) studio units, nineteen (19) one-bedroom units, thirteen (13) two-bedroom units, and five (5) three-bedroom units.

Boston.name: 3458 Washington Street
Boston.description: Propose to construct a new five-story building to contain approximately 807 square feet of ground-floor commercial space and 36 dwelling units, 7 motor vehicle exterior surface parking spaces, and bicycle parking/storage in accordance with City requirements.

Boston.name: 257 Washington Street
Boston.description: The proposed building will consist of approximately 49,979 gross square feet and is four stories with a below-ground garage level for parking and bike storage. The parking garage is accessed via a new curb cut on Washington Street and has 26 total parking spaces. In the rear of the garage level is a bike room with 70 total bicycle parking spaces, as well as a trash room and mechanical and storage space. The first level of the building consists of retail space and residential space.

Boston.name: 376-384A Blue Hill Avenue
Boston.description: MTK Development proposes to develop a 4-story building with ground floor retail and community space, 3 floors of residential units, and rooftop green space and Solar PV. The 18 residential units are comprised of 1BD, 2BD, and 3BD units that will be targeting households between 80%-100% AMI. Currently, all of the units and commercial space will be for sale, however, the programming can change depending on community feedback and feasibility.

Boston.name: 1690-1700 Hyde Park Avenue
Boston.description: Project proposal is to create 115 multi-family rental units with approximately 99,000 gross square feet of floor area, including 1,500 gsf of ground floor supporting retail uses, 69 garage parking spaces, widened public sidewalk, new open space, and related amenities on a 30,860 square foot (0.71 acre) site in the Hyde Park neighborhood of Boston.

Boston.name: 3430 & 3440 Washington Street
Boston.description: The proposal is in the PLAN: JP/Rox study area and calls for two separate (divided by Rockvale circle) mixed-use residential/commercial multi-family buildings to replace the existing auto body repair shop and gas station.

Boston.name: 434 Washington Street
Boston.description: Raze existing structure; erect a new four-story mixed-use building with eighteen (18) residential units, one (1) 1,180 sf ground floor commercial retail space, twenty-four (24) bicycle spaces, and eleven (11) interior parking spaces.

Boston.name: On the Square
Boston.description: OTS is a new development project that will transform approximately 10,000 square feet of existing retail office building into a new mixed-use building in Codman Square. The project will demolish the existing building and garage in an adjacent lot to construct a new five-story mixed use commercial/residential containing 73,472 square feet of office/residential space. The commercial/retail space will bring back some existing tenants of the current building and will potentially add new retail tenants. The residential portion of the building will include 41 affordable rental units to families with incomes below 60% AMI. There will be 14 one-bedroom units, 23 two bed units and 4 three bed units available for these tenants.

Boston.name: 290 Tremont Street
Boston.description:
The Project consists of the construction of a new twelve-story, mixed-income residential development of approximately 127,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area (as calculated pursuant to the code, “GFA”) of income-restricted rental housing and approximately 3,000 square feet of GFA of ground floor space dedicated to a community/commercial use (“Project”). The Project will advance the City’s 2030 Housing Plan's housing creation goals and introduce “development without displacement” in a neighborhood with limited development opportunities.

When completed, the Project will significantly enhance the stock of income-restricted rental and homeownership housing available in the Chinatown neighborhood. The Project will include approximately one hundred eleven (111) rental apartments restricted to income-eligible renters.

Boston.name: 749-759 Dudley Street
Boston.description: The proposed mixed-use commercial/multi-family residential development will be constructed on a 9,908 sf existing commercial site in the Dorchester, Uphams Corner neighborhood with 3,500 gsf of ground floor commercial space along with 48 multi-family units, with 9-garage and 52-bicycle spaces, and having a total of 49,114 gsf of floor area in a new 6-story building.

Boston.name: 495 Dorchester Avenue
Boston.description: The Project calls for the construction of a new 237-unit market rate, 16-story residential building and a new 7-story, 94-unit income-restricted midrise building for seniors joined by a shared podium. The Proposed Project will contain approximately 326,000 square feet of gross floor area, including approximately 11,710 square feet of ground-floor retail / commercial space and 88 below-grade parking spaces. The senior mid-rise building will have dedicated amenities and services common to service-enriched senior housing as well as full access to shared amenities within the planned community, such as a gym, social activities, retail services, and newly created open space. The programming will include supportive services to enhance the resident experience and quality of life and to maintain independent living as they age. Rogerson Communities has agreed to be the services partner for the Project and will bring its very thorough program of services coordination and dedicated and community-based services to this senior community.

Boston.name: 1274 Massachusetts Avenue
Boston.description:
The Proposed Project is a mixed-use development consisting of a 6 story building containing 45
residential units, approximately 1,000 square feet of ground floor commercial space, a public
landscaped plaza space, 46 bike storage spaces, and 25 accessory off-street parking spaces located
in the building’s basement level enclosed parking garage.

Boston.name: 23-25 North Beacon Street
Boston.description:
The proposed project includes the demolition of an existing three-story residential structure and the construction of a six-story, twenty-five (25) unit multi-family building. The new building will include thirteen (13) one-bedroom units, three (3) two-bedroom units and nine (9) three-bedroom units. 

The development will replace an existing parking area at the rear of the site with shared open space for building residents, reducing impervious surface and increasing usable green space.

Boston.name: 662-666 East Broadway
Boston.description: Erect new four-story mixed-use building to contain one ground-floor commercial unit and 21 residential condominium units on floor two through four, with 15 garage parking spaces.

Boston.name: 281 Franklin Street
Boston.description: The proposed project at 281 Franklin Street is part of the BPDA's Office to Residential Conversion Program. The project proposes the renovation and change in use for the existing 11,119 sq ft mixed-use building from Ground-Floor Restaurant and Offices above to Ground-Floor Restaurant and 15 residential apartment units above. Including 10 studio units and 5 one-bedroom units. With 3 IDP units (20% of proposed units).

Boston.name: 944 Saratoga Street
Boston.description: The project proposes 21 rental units with 11 parking spaces, and 28 bicycle spaces. The proposed project site is currently vacant and was previously occupied by a one-story auto garage.

Boston.name: 20 Charlesgate West
Boston.description: The proposed Our Lady’s Guild House (“OLGH”) project by Fenway CDC and the Planning Office for Urban Affairs includes the complete renovation and modernization of a 140-room lodging house into an 86-unit rental building in the Kenmore Square neighborhood. This Project is the culmination of years of advocacy on behalf of residents to purchase the building and return it to its original mission of providing affordable housing. The 6-story elevator building will include 22 enhanced permanent supportive housing Single Room Occupancy (“SRO”) apartments, 45 studio apartments, 19 one-bedroom apartments, a community room with kitchen and storage, an office, lounge, laundry facilities, other ancillary spaces, and bicycle parking.  The Project and neighborhood are extraordinarily well situated because of the Project’s proximity to transportation, medical facilities, shopping, places of worship, recreational facilities, places of employment, and other necessary services for the prospective residents.

Boston.name: 841 Morton Street
Boston.description: Moawed Properties LLC (the "Proponent") proposes to redevelop an approximately 21,985 square-foot Project Site, which is currently occupied by a gas station that includes a one-story brick building, associated gas pumps under a canopy, paved parking areas, dumpster area, and landscaped areas with access from both Morton and Flint Streets into a new 5-story mixed-use, multi-family residence with approximately 67,567 gross square feet of floor area including 52 residential units, approximately 2,396 gross square feet of ground floor retail space, amenity spaces for residents, a 35 parking space garage, 42 bicycle spaces within the building, and additional exterior bicycle spaces for visitors in conformance with City guidelines (collectively, the "Proposed Project").

Boston.name: 77 Terrace Street
Boston.description: 48 units of affordable ownership to be constructed on City of Boston land following tentative designation by City/MOH. The Project will create 48 units of ownership housing (80% and 100% of Boston AMI) along with approximately 2,000 sf of ground-floor retail with garage parking. The building is located between Parker Street and Terrace Street in the Mission Hill neighborhood of Boston.

Boston.name: 29-33 Romsey Street
Boston.description: The Proposed Project calls for the demolition of the existing, vacant structures on the 25,271 square foot site at 29 - 33 Romsey Street, to allow for the construction of a new, two-building residential development including seven (7) townhouses and a twenty-two (22) unit residential building, of which twelve (12) units will be income-restricted affordable units.

Boston.name: 736-742 East Broadway Mixed-Use Project
Boston.description: Erect a new four-story building to contain 12 dwelling units, with a ground-floor restaurant and six off-street garage parking spaces.

Boston.name: 101 Boston Street
Boston.description: The Proponent proposes the revitalization of this underutilized Project Site with the construction of a new six (6) story, multifamily residential building of up to approximately 49,900 square feet of total Gross Floor Area (“GFA”), with up to 59 units of residential housing, associated residential indoor and outdoor amenity spaces, a ground floor restaurant/takeout restaurant and/or retail space of up to approximately 2,211 square feet, and up to ten (10) onsite vehicular garaged parking spaces with access from an existing curb cut along the Frontage Road, along with related improvements in pedestrian accessibility, landscape, and public realm improvements in and around the Project Site, consistent with the character and housing needs of the surrounding community.

Boston.name: 112-114 Queensberry Street
Boston.description: Fenway CDC plans to develop the 112-114 Queensberry site, located in the western section of Boston’s Fenway neighborhood, into 24 units of affordable housing. Fenway CDC proposes to construct a building with six stories above grade and one story partially below grade. 100% of the units will be affordable in perpetuity. The units will be affordable to individuals and households at or below 30% and 60% of area median income. The building will include a mix of studios and one-bedrooms to provide housing for single people, couples, and small families. No parking will be provided onsite.

Boston.name: West End Library
Boston.description: Preservation of Affordable Housing, Inc. (POAH) and Caste Capital, LLC (Caste) will redevelop the West End Library into 119 units of affordable housing, community space, and a new West End branch of the Boston Public Library. We envision the transformation of a beloved community resource into a welcoming, spacious library alongside a sustainable, diverse, intergenerational affordable housing community.

Boston.name: Austin Street Lots Redevelopment
Boston.description: The Project Site is comprised of discrete City of Boston Assessing Parcel Nos. 0203964000 and 0203963050, located at the southwestern corner of the intersection of New Rutherford Avenue and Austin Street in Charlestown, currently containing two surface parking lots. The project consists of four new mixed-use buildings collectively containing up to 790,000 sf of Gross Floor Area and delivering up to 705 new dwelling units and residential amenities, arts and culture space, early childhood education space, indoor recreation space, and structured and/or surface vehicle parking spaces, together with an urban plaza and lawn and athletic/multipurpose fields, and related site and public realm improvements.

Boston.name: 279-283 North Harvard Street
Boston.description: The proposed project would raze the existing distressed single-family dwelling and preserve, repurpose, and expand the existing structure of the Hill Memorial Baptist Church into a four (4) story building with 49 units of income-restricted senior housing units and a new connected structure with program space for the residents of the new development (the “Proposed Project”). The basement of the former church building will provide a public space for continued and enhanced community use, and the overall development program will incorporate an extensive array of open spaces, with at-grade surface parking for 15 vehicles accessed from Easton Street.

Boston.name: 75-77 Dorchester Street
Boston.description: The proposed project consists of a new five-story mixed-use building at 75-77 Dorchester Street in the South Boston neighborhood. The new building will contain 15 residential rental units, including income-restricted affordable units pursuant to Article 79’s Inclusionary Zoning requirements. There will also be 8 off-site parking spaces allocated to this proposal within the abutting privately owned parking lot. The project site includes 4,330 square feet of land area, comprising situated at 75-77 Dorchester Street in South Boston, being City of Boston Assessor’s Parcel No. 0601886000 and City of Boston Assessor’s Parcel No. 0601887000. The Dorchester Street parcels are currently the site of a one story restaurant, STATS Bar and Grill and a two-family dwelling. The project site is currently within a Multifamily/Local Services zoning subdistrict under Article 68, the South Boston Neighborhood Zoning Article.

Boston.name: 85 Devonshire Street
Boston.description: Conversion of three (3) adjoining buildings from business use to residential apartments in accordance with the Downtown Residential Conversion Incentive Pilot Program, combining them into one (1) singular building. The buildings include 85 Devonshire Street, 258 Washington Street, and 262 Washington Street. This conversion will provide Ninety-Five (95) residential rental apartments and amenities, from Floor Two (2) to Floor Eleven (11), totaling approximately 86,700 square feet, and approximately 15,798 square feet of retail will remain on the first floor and mezzanine levels. The unit mix will be comprised of twenty-nine (29) studio apartments, fifty-four (54) one-bedroom apartments, and twelve (12) two-bedroom apartments, with an average unit area of six-hundred and forty (640) square feet.

Boston.name: 99-105 Addison Street
Boston.description: The Proponent proposes to revitalize the Project Site with a new multi-family development that is consistent with the character and context of the surrounding community. The proposed project would upgrade the Project Site with a coastal flood resilient four-story, 20 unit residential development that includes 10 on-site garaged parking spaces, 22 bike spaces, new sidewalk, pedestrian access, landscaping, open space, public realm and overall site improvements.

Boston.name: 1740 Hyde Park Avenue
Boston.description: Proposing to construct a new 5 story residential building with 42 units and 19 parking spaces.

Boston.name: 24 Mt. Everett Street
Boston.description: The proposal consists of a renovation and addition to the existing structure. The addition will be three (3) stories and contain a total unit count of sixteen (16) with sixteen (16) vehicular parking spaces.

Boston.name: 639 Warren Street
Boston.description: 639 Warren Street is a proposed new construction project from Madison Park Development Corporation for a currently vacant lot located at the corner of Warren and Crawford Streets in the Grove Hall neighborhood of Boston. The proposed Notice of Project Change will feature a mixture of commercial and residential rental uses, fully affordable to incomes ranging from 30-80% AMI. This project will provide affordable housing to a total of 63 households near a dynamic commercial center with access to numerous transit lines (including bus and commuter rail), along with space for local businesses or nonprofit use.

Boston.name: Rogerson-Beaufort
Boston.description:
The Rogerson-Beaufort project will be located on a Rogerson Communities property in Jamaica Plain that is currently the home of a 66-bed licensed Assisted Living memory care community and a Social Day program for seniors with memory loss. Rogerson Communities is proposing a two-phased redevelopment of the 3.2-acre site located on the Jamaicaway.  The campus overlooks Jamaica Pond and is within walking distance of public transportation, restaurants, grocery stores, and other retail and health services.

The first phase of development will occur while the existing Assisted Living community and Social Day program remain fully operational. On an undeveloped portion at the rear of the property, the Rogerson-Beaufort project will develop a single building that will replace the memory care community and the Social Day program and will add affordable housing for seniors.  A second phase of development will add additional affordable apartments for seniors and community spaces after the rear portion of the existing memory care building is demolished, leaving the front lawns fully intact.

In the first phase, we are planning 41 affordable independent living senior apartments that will benefit from Rogerson Communities’ full offerings of supportive services for seniors.  Those services include Resident Services Coordinators, programmed group activities, community services, and amenities such as exercise programs, computer learning, and wellness coordination with other supportive service providers. 
Rogerson Communities is committed to developing buildings and a campus on our Jamaica Plain site that will be sustainable and environmentally sensitive and will add to the vibrancy of the community with beautiful outdoor spaces along with connection to and activation of our campus for both our residents and neighbors.

Boston.name: 2062 Dorchester Avenue
Boston.description: The proposed project consists of twenty new residential units, primarily market rate, with affordable units to be provided pursuant to the requirements of Article 79. The new building will include five below-grade motor vehicle parking spaces, ample secure bicycle storage, and will feature significant residential amenity space and site enhancements.

Boston.name: 39 Minot Street
Boston.description: The proposal intends to renovate and add a rear addition to the existing two-family building on the site, while preserving the historical structure. The project will also add two new residential buildings, on each side of the existing structure, thereby creating 24 additional units with 20 off-street parking spaces.

Boston.name: 34-36 Pratt Street
Boston.description: The proposed development at 34-36 Pratt Street in Allston would replace two residential buildings with a six-story, approximately 39-unit multi-family residential building. The project includes seven affordable units, a parking garage with 11 parking spaces, and approximately 40 bike parking spaces.

Boston.name: 98-100 Condor Street
Boston.description: The Proposed Project would reprogram the entire existing structure from a vacant industrial/commercial use to 35 new residential rental units. In connection with the Proposed Project, there will be seven (7) accessory off-street surface parking spaces. In addition, Project Amenities will include an on-site fitness room, bike storage for 44 bikes, building gathering space, laundry room, bike storage room, and storage lockers.

Boston.name: 11-11 A Parker Hill Avenue
Boston.description: The Proposed Project is to construct a six (6) story, seventy-one (71) unit addition to the rear of the existing apartment building at 11 Parker Hill Ave. The existing building will undergo no changes other than updates to the façade to better match the new addition. The addition will include seven (7) vehicular parking spaces, eighty-six (86) total bicycle parking spaces, a fitness room amenity, and a roof deck amenity. Vehicular parking will be located below grade, internal to the building, and will be accessed via a relocated curb cut along Parker Hill Ave

Boston.name: 84 Stonley Road
Boston.description: The project proposes construction of a 5-story building with 28 rental units (5 of which will be affordable). The building will fill the lot along Stonley Road and Stedman Street, defining the existing street wall and creating a gateway between the two streets. The building is within walking distance of both MBTA Orange Line Forest Hills and Green Street stations, as well as MBTA bus routes along Washington Street. The project proposes no parking.

Boston.name: 586-598 Canterbury Street
Boston.description: A residential development, approximately 46,021 SF of Gross Area, comprised of 46 units and 32 Parking spaces

Boston.name: 129 Portland Street
Boston.description: The proposed project at 129 Portland Street is part of the Office to Residential Conversion Program. The proposal seeks to convert the existing office space in the 6-story 28k sf building with ground-level retail located at the corner of Portland Street and Valenti Way in the Bulfinch Triangle, creating 25 new units of residential including a mix of studios, 1-bedroom, 2-bedrooms, and 3-bedrooms. The new residential sf being created totals 22,005 gfa. Conversion requires minimal exterior facade work

Boston.name: 3716-3724 Washington Street
Boston.description: Proposal to redevelop the site located at 3716-3724 Washington Street. Site currently contains a single story retail building that would be razed. Construction proposed for a new six story mixed-use building with 2 first floor retail units and 35 residential units.

Boston.name: 65-79 Seattle Street
Boston.description: A mixed-income development with forty-three (43) homeownership units of which twenty-two (22) of the units will be restricted to households earning at or below 80% AMI, and twenty-one (21) of the units will be restricted to households earning at or below 100% AMI. The project is broken up into three separate buildings and capped at three (3) stories. The project provides 15,000 sf of open space, and an internal walkway underneath that connects the site to the future greenway.

Boston.name: 575 Albany Street
Boston.description: On July 5, 2024, the Proponent submitted a Notice of Project Change (the “July 2024 NPC”) further updating the Project by changing the use of portions of the first floor of the building from commercial to residential uses as shown on the floor plans attached hereto as Exhibit A (the “Floor Plans”) and reducing the total number of homeownership units in the building from approximately 50 to approximately 44 (collectively, the “Proposed Changes”). As shown on the Floor Plans, the ground-floor commercial space has been further reduced to approximately 1,100 square feet of commercial space, and the six ground-floor units have been relocated and replaced with the following components: one market rate unit, five affordable units for occupancy by artists pursuant to the Mayor Office of Arts and Culture’s​ (“MOAC”)​ Artist Certification process (“Artist Live/Work Units”). The total gross floor area, height, dimensions and building design remain consistent with the description of the Project previously approved and described in the Development Plan. No other changes to the Project are proposed.

Boston.name: 329 Blue Hill Avenue
Boston.description:
329 Blue Hill Avenue is a proposed five-story, 40-unit, income-restricted family rental development located along Boston’s Blue Hill Avenue corridor in the Dorchester/Roxbury area of Suffolk County. The project is planned as new construction on an approximately 23,708-square-foot (0.54-acre), currently vacant site that is owned by Caribbean Integration Community Development.
The proposed building will contain approximately 49,620 gross square feet, including approximately 47,020 square feet of residential space and approximately 2,600 square feet of commercial space. The project will transform an underutilized, privately owned vacant parcel into a mixed-use development that expands the supply of permanently income-restricted family housing while creating neighborhood-serving commercial space along a major community corridor.

Boston.name: 776 Summer Street - Phase 2
Boston.description: The 776 Summer Street Phase 2 Project encompasses key components of the PDA Master Plan, including the construction of two residential buildings on Blocks A and B (Including up to 636 units across Blocks A, B, and E) with parking and ground floor retail; a hotel/residential building on Block E and the 1898 Building, offering up to 240 keys, along with parking, amenities, and ground floor retail; a research and development building at Block C with associated parking and ground floor retail; and the implementation of Phase 2 site improvements, such as portions of Edison Plaza (formerly M Street Plaza), public realm enhancements on Summer Street, East First Street, and Thomas Edison Way, and supporting Phase 2 infrastructure.

Boston.name: North Station Gateway Project
Boston.description: The Project proposes the construction of an approximately 40-story mixed-use building of approximately 560,000 SF of Gross Floor Area (GFA) and approximately 447 feet in height. The development program consists of approximately 300 hotel rooms, approximately 420 residential units, approximately 30,000 SF of retail, restaurant and amenity space. The Project will also include a rooftop mechanical penthouse and approximately 150 parking spaces across two levels of below-grade parking.

Boston.name: 265 Maverick Street
Boston.description: Reuse of existing garage on 10,000 square foot lot.  Change occupancy to multifamily residential building with 36 Residential Units, 13 garage parking spaces, bike storage and building amenities at ground level.  Project to include ground level design to comply with Coastal Flood Resiliency Overlay District ("CFROD").

Boston.name: 259-267 Summer Street
Boston.description: Convert existing office building to mixed-use building, to contain approximately 77 dwelling units, with amenity space, and approximately 3 commercial/retail units, as part of the Office to Residential Conversion Pilot program.

Boston.name: 80 Gardner Street
Boston.description: The proposed project involves the construction of a new six-story, multi-family residential building comprising 36 units. The existing site currently includes 23 vehicular parking spaces, which will be retained. An additional 20 parking spaces are proposed as part of the new development, along with 50 bicycle parking spaces to support sustainable transportation options.

Boston.name: Shawmut Avenue / Washington Street Block Project
Boston.description: Beacon Communities LLC (“Beacon”) and the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association of New England, Inc. (“CCBA” and together with Beacon, the “Proponent”) propose to construct a seven story, approximately 105 foot high building on the Project Site; the building will contain approximately 168,500 gross square foot of area comprising approximately 117 rental apartment units (all of which shall be affordable), approximately 22,000 square feet of basement commercial space that could accommodate an urban grocery store, and approximately 2,350 square feet of ground floor commercial space that will face Washington Street;  an at-grade indoor parking area for approximately 20 vehicles for the commercial space, as well as residential amenity spaces such as a resident community room, property management offices, a mailroom, laundry facilities, and a bicycle room that will have storage space for bicycles at a ratio of 1 bicycle/unit and an additional  bicycle space for management staff.

Boston.name: 1214 Bennington Street
Boston.description: Renovate existing structure and erect vertical addition.  Change occupancy to 28 residential units with garage parking for 10 vehicles and 34 bike spaces.

Boston.name: 350 West Fourth Street
Boston.description: Redevelopment of a 43,996 square-foot Project Site which is currently occupied by an accessory surface parking to the adjacent Bigelow Condominium Building (“Bigelow”). The proposed multi-family, 4-story residential development will include 35 units, with 75 basement and ground floor garage parking spaces to serve the existing Bigelow building and the Project, and will contain 46 indoor resident bike spaces and 10 exterior visitor bike spaces.

Boston.name: 15 Court Square
Boston.description: Conversion of an existing eleven (11) story office building in Boston Proper into a residential use with eighty (80) rental units. Residential units will comprise all floors above Ground Level and Lower Level retail spaces, which will remain as is. No Off-Street Parking will be provided

Boston.name: 261 Maverick Street
Boston.description: Erect addition to existing structures and change occupancy from office to retail and multifamily residential containing 24 units.  Ground level to contain 2,700 square feet of retail, bike storage, building amenity and six (6) surface parking spaces.  Building to be designed in accordance with Article 25A (Coastal Flood Resiliency Overlay District).

Boston.name: 2-8 Bowdoin Street
Boston.description:
The proposed project sits on a single lot with a total area of 4,380 square feet. The site is located at 2-8 Bowdoin Street, on the prominent corner at the intersection of Bowdoin Street, Washington Street, and Harvard Street in the Four Corners neighborhood of Dorchester. The project entails the construction of a seven-story building comprising 22 residential units, 2,400 square feet of commercial/restaurant space, and 1,500 square feet of shared tenant amenities, including bike parking, storage space, and an accessible roof deck for all building residents. Residents and restaurant visitors will access the proposed building from Bowdoin Street, while the trash room and bike storage access will be located off Bowdoin Avenue. 

This project is located within a ten-minute walk (0.4 mile) of the Four Corners/Geneva MBTA Commuter Rail Station, is adjacent to bus route 23 along Washington St and within a 15-minute walk to the Fields Corner Red Line T Stop.

The proponent aims to revitalize the square and attract businesses back to the immediate area. The proposed ground floor is set back from the property line to create a continuous overhang, illuminating the immediate sidewalk and adjacent areas to foster a safer environment for local residents at night. These public realm improvements, coupled with sidewalk upgrades and planted street trees, are intended to enhance vibrancy and attract local visitors to the area.

Boston.name: 1028-1032 Dorchester Avenue
Boston.description: The Proponent proposes a new 4 Story mixed-use building, comprised of 5,309 SF of ground floor retail space, 12 parking  spaces and 22 residential units.

Boston.name: 697 Cambridge Street
Boston.description:
The proposed development at 697 Cambridge Street has been designed to transform an existing two- story commercial structure into a five-story multifamily residential building while maintaining compatibility with its urban context. The program organizes residential, parking, and support spaces to create a functional and efficient structure that responds to the character of the section of Cambridge Street on which the site sits.

The building will contain 42 residential units organized across the lower level through the fifth floor. The unit mix is designed to support a diversity of household types, including 17 studios, 15 one-bedroom units, 7 two-bedroom units, and 3 three-bedroom units. Many units will benefit from exclusive-use balconies, offering residents private outdoor space. Interior layouts have been planned to maximize natural light, efficiency, and livability.

Boston.name: Great Scott Redevelopment
Boston.description: The proposed project is focused on reviving Allston’s legendary Great Scott music venue, which closed during the COVID-19 pandemic. It consists of the demolition of the existing structures occupying the site and the construction of a mixed-use building occupying approximately 97,300 square feet of gross floor area with approximately 139 rental residential units on the upper floors, and a ground level featuring a new, 300-person capacity performance space for Great Scott, the retention of O’Brien’s Pub, additional retail/commercial space, and off-street parking spaces for three car-sharing vehicles.

Boston.name: 4 Liberty Square
Boston.description: The proposed project at 4 Liberty Square consists of the renovation of the existing +-25,000 Sq ft 7 story office building with restaurant space on the ground level which sits prominently on Liberty Square at the corner of Batterymarch & Water Street. The proposed plans call for the existing office space on floors 2-7 to be converted to apartments. This would create 36 new units. Of those units 5 IDP units and 1 voucher unit are proposed. Restaurant or retail use would remain on the ground level.

Boston.name: 265 Hancock Street
Boston.description: The Proposed Project will  construct a new 6-story mixed-use building with approximately 24 residential rental units, 28 bicycle parking spaces, and ground floor retail space.

Boston.name: 19-21 West Third Street
Boston.description: The proposed project consists of a new six-story mixed-use building at 19-21 West Third Street in the Broadway Station area of South Boston. The new building will contain thirty-five residential condominium units for sale, including 17% income-restricted affordable units pursuant to Article 79’s Inclusionary Zoning requirements. One ground-floor commercial unit of approximately 821 square feet will be provided along with garage parking for ten motor vehicles, as well as secure storage for thirty-five bicycles.

Boston.name: Longwood Place Phase One
Boston.description: The proposed project includes the initial project components within the approved Longwood Place PDA Development Plan, including Commercial Building 1 (formerly known as Building 1), Commercial Building 2 (formerly known as Building 3), Residential Building 1 (formerly known as Building 4), below-grade parking and loading, and associated site improvements, including landscaping and public realm improvements.

Boston.name: 1428 Dorchester Avenue
Boston.description:
The proposed project consists of 23 new residential apartments, primarily
market rate, including 17% affordable units to be provided pursuant to the
requirements of Inclusionary Zoning, Article 79 of the Boston Zoning Code. The
proposed project is located in the heart of the Fields Corner neighborhood within the Dorchester Avenue corridor, making the approximately 7,747 square foot project site
ideally suited for new residential development. Architectural services are being
provided by Context Workshop of Boston.

Boston.name: 25 Tolman Street
Boston.description: 25 Tolman street utilizes the footprint and height-profile of the existing structure and an ample 22,670 square foot lot to construct seventeen (17) total home-ownership units, each with its own parking space.  The units are a combination of townhouses and apartment-style units, and are spread out within three different structures, with six (6) units in the Tolman Street apartment building, and the remaining eleven (11) townhouses in the rear portion of the lot.  In addition, a second driveway will be constructed off Morrissey Boulevard so as not to burden Tolman Street.  The density of the lot is below a Floor Area Ratio of 1.0, intended to reflect the massing of nearby structures.

Boston.name: 201 Hampden Street
Boston.description:
201 Hampden Street was previously approved as a five-story, approximately 20,430-square-foot condominium development containing 13 market-rate residential units under Building Permit ERT 959528. The site has remained vacant and unimproved for more than 30 years.

In response to evolving housing needs and market conditions, the proposed project seeks to increase the number of residential units while remaining substantially within the previously approved zoning envelope. The revised proposal maintains the approved building height and features a smaller overall building footprint and gross floor area, while introducing a more efficient unit mix and floor plan layout that increases housing production. The project will provide 24 homeownership units, including three Income-Restricted Units, helping to address Boston's housing shortage while delivering a high-performance, transit-oriented residential building adjacent to Dudley Town Common.

Boston.name: 1200 Centre Street
Boston.description: Hebrew SeniorLife (HSL) proposes to build a 78-unit affordable senior housing community in partnership with the BHA/HUD through the Restore Rebuild program. The project will be located at the corner of Centre Street and Walter Street in Roslindale on a site owned and operated by HSL. The HSL campus includes a comprehensive healthcare and research facility that provides a range of services to seniors, from rehabilitation and outpatient care to end-of-life support. The proposed development will repurpose an existing parking lot, comprising 0.78 acres of the 9.4-acre site. The proposed 6-story building will include 78 deeply affordable senior housing units, composed of seventy-four one-bedroom units and four two-bedroom units. There will be shared amenity spaces that include staff offices, a multi-purpose room, a wellness room, a reception area/lobby, mail and package rooms, a library, a bike storage room, and a fitness room. Residents accessing the common amenity space at level 6 will be able to enjoy the view down Centre Street, expansive views of the Arboretum, and of the City skyline.

Boston.name: 151 Lenox Street
Boston.description:
151 Lenox Street is an approximately 4,692 square foot vacant parcel known as Parcel 22A located in Roxbury. The Parcel is currently licensed by the BPDA to the nearby People’s Baptist Church for parking and now tentatively designated to Tenants Development Corporation (“TDC”). The site was historically occupied by residential and commercial properties (a hotel, carpenter shop, miscellaneous storage).
TDC proposes a 38 unit senior, all affordable LIHTC development. The development is proposed as 7 stories, with two elevators, and 31,805 gsf with a façade which will blend into the surrounding community. The first floor will include a lobby, mailroom, common community room with a warming kitchen, a laundry room, a bike room, and a management office. TDC will seek third party management with greater experience in senior housing and supportive service provision.

Boston.name: 123 North Washington Street
Boston.description: The proposed project at 123 North Washington Street is part of the Office to Residential Conversion Program. The Proponent (Copper Mill North End, LLC) is proposing to convert the existing five story office building to residential use. The proposed building will have 45 units and ground floor retail.

Boston.name: 1 & 10 Emerson Place
Boston.description: Conversion of approximately 20,060 sf of office space within existing Emerson Place buildings into 33 residential apartment units

Boston.name: 1 Longfellow Place
Boston.description: Conversion of approximately 13,164 sf of office space into a total of 24 residential apartment units pursuant to the City's office to residential conversion program.

Boston.name: 62-66 Condor Street
Boston.description: Erect new 5 story mixed use retail and multi family residential building on 20,574 square foot lot.  Building to include 15 parking spaces, bike storage, ground level building amenities and retail space, 36 residential units and a common roof deck.  Project is subject to Article 80E-2 (Small Project).

Boston.name: 16-18 Hawley Street
Boston.description: Office to Residential conversion of an existing 11-story office condominium at the Project Site (“Unit 2”) from a commercial/office/business use to residential apartments in accordance with the Downtown Office to Residential Conversion Pilot Program (the “Pilot Program”), with Unit 2 consisting of approximately 86,730 square feet of Gross Floor Area (“GFA”) and approximately and 95,037 Gross Square Feet (“GSF”) (the “Project”).  The Project will provide one hundred and ten (110) residential rental apartments floors two (2) to eleven (11) and associated amenities in the building’s mezzanine and basement. The existing Retail Use on the first floor (Unit 1, separately owned and leased to the US Postal Service for a Post Office) will remain unchanged, as will the exterior of the building. The unit mix will be comprised of twenty (20) studio apartments, seventy-two (72) one-bedroom apartments, and eighteen (18) two-bedroom apartments.

Boston.name: 9 Chelsea Street
Boston.description: The Proposed Project consists of a new six-story, mixed-use residential building containing approximately 83,223  gross square feet, 121 residential rental units, and approximately 4,729 square feet of ground floor retail and commercial space, together with widened sidewalks, open space, and related site and building amenities. The 109 residential units are proposed to be a diverse mix of types including: 18-two-bedroom, 28-one-bedroom and 75-studio units. The first floor will provide amenity space for residents to utilize in accordance with Planning Department policy, and a 3,279 square foot rooftop deck for residents. No basement space will be provided.

Boston.name: 295-297 Franklin Street
Boston.description: The proposed project is contemplated as part of the Downtown Office to Residential Conversion Program and consists of the re-use of a pre-existing five (5) story building located at 295-297 Franklin Street in downtown Boston from its present occupancy of commercial space on the ground floor, and upper-story offices, to approximately 744 square feet of ground floor retail and eighteen (18) new dwelling units on floors one through five.  Located in the B-10 Zoning Subdistrict, the site consists of a 2,430 square foot lot with existing gross floor area of 14,580 square feet, which includes a basement to be re-purposed for bike storage and other building services.

Boston.name: 201-207 Brighton Avenue
Boston.description: 201 Brighton Avenue LLC proposes to redevelop the approximately 27,516 square-foot Project Site into a new six-story mixed-use building containing approximately 145 new residential apartment units and approximately 1,993 square feet of ground-floor commercial space, altogether totaling approximately 104,036 square feet of gross floor area (the “Proposed Project”). The Proposed Project also includes 145 secure interior bicycle spaces on the ground floor as well as 31 exterior visitor bicycle spaces, and will feature a landscaped open space and sitting area, and along with a new sidewalk connecting the site with Cambridge Street. Pursuant to the Inclusionary Zoning (“IZ”) requirements of Article 79 of the Boston Zoning Code, the Proposed Project’s IZ commitment will include a minimum of 20% of Units/Usable Square Footage, if ultimately approved as a rental project. The Project Site consists of two parcels and contains a total lot area of approximately 27,516 square feet, situated along Brighton Avenue with a portion of the rear of the property abutting on Cambridge Street (the “Project Site”). The Project Site’s existing conditions include a one-story commercial structure for the Action Bearing Company and 10 parallel surface parking spaces.

Boston.name: 12 Post Office Square
Boston.description: 12 Post Office Square, LLC, proposes the conversion of two adjoining six-story buildings, located at 12 Post Office Square and 10 Liberty Square, from their present occupancies of basement and ground-floor retail and commercial uses, and upper-story offices, to basement and ground-floor retail and commercial uses with seventy (70) new dwelling units on floors two through six, with approximately two thousand square feet of residential amenity space.

Boston.name: 92 Spring Street
Boston.description: The Proposed Project is to construct a new four (4) story residential building, composed of forty-four (44) residential units and accessory parking below grade at the basement level. A total of forty-four (44) parking spaces will be provided. Two existing parcels will be combined to form the project site creating a 22,890 square foot lot. The Proposed Project will be approximately 48,463 square feet in Gross Square Feet.

Boston.name: 3841 Washington Street
Boston.description: Erect a new seven-story mixed-use building to contain approximately 165 dwelling units, including Inclusionary Zoning units in accordance with the requirements of Article 79, and approximately 5,652 square feet of ground-floor commercial space, with thirty-three garage parking spaces. secure indoor bicycle storage, and exterior visitor bicycle racks.

Boston.name: 1576 Blue Hill Avenue
Boston.description: The proposed project will construct a new 6-story mixed-use building (the “New Building”) with a total of fifty-eight (58) residential units for lease (consisting of one-, two-, and three- bedroom units), approximately 1842 sf of ground-floor retail space, a minimum of four (4) parking spaces, potentially more with the use of stackers, twenty-four (24) indoor bicycle parking spaces, outdoor amenity space and related site improvements (the “Proposed Project”). The New Building will consist of approximately 47,878 gross square feet.

Boston.name: 15 Supertest Street
Boston.description: The proposed project at 15 Supertest Street will include up to approximately 24,000 square feet of retail space addressing Rutherford Avenue and Supertest Streets, proposed as a single retail use. On the second and third levels, the project proposes eighteen (18) affordable rental residential units in three-bedroom and four-bedroom “family” configurations, as “off-site” IDP units from the 25 Supertest tower project (filed concurrently but separately).

Boston.name: 69 McGreevey Way
Boston.description:
Mission Main Tenant Task Force and WinnDevelopment are partnering to develop Ward Street Senior Housing, a 110-unit, 100% deeply affordable ground-up development for seniors aged 62 and older in Boston’s Mission Hill neighborhood. Resident rents will not exceed 30% of housing income. The development will feature approximately 77 one-bedroom and 33 two-bedroom apartments and is designed to support independent living for low-income elderly households. 

This joint venture builds on a decades-long partnership and the successful transformation of the Mission Main Apartments, a 535-unit affordable housing community co-owned and co-managed by the Tenant Task Force. The new senior housing development will expand the overall number of affordable homes at Mission Main from 445 to 567, helping residents age in place while freeing up family-sized units for other households on the BHA waitlist. 

The project will incorporate Passive House sustainability standards, Universal Design accessibility, and strong resident service programming. It will also enhance connectivity to nearby public transit and green spaces. Special focus will be placed on serving both elderly residents and grandparents raising grandchildren, with tailored programs to support their well-being and economic needs. 

Ward Street Senior Housing is designed to reflect inclusive growth, racial and economic equity, and long-term affordability. The development team is committed to exceeding goals for MBE/WBE and Section 3 participation, drawing on successful strategies from recent work at Mission Main. 

Resident engagement and empowerment remain central to the vision, with planning and management informed by the lived experience and leadership of the Mission Main Tenant Task Force. The project is a model for equitable, community-driven senior housing in Boston.

Boston.name: 52 Plympton Street
Boston.description:
The proposed development at 52 Plympton Street would replace two underutilized buildings with a seven-story, approximately 44-unit multi-family residential building located in the South End’s EDA South sub-district and in the Protection Area of the South End Landmark District. 

The project includes a fully accessible ground floor artist live-work component comprising eight affordable live-work units designed specifically to support artists, paired with a multi-purpose gallery and workshop space with direct access to a rear courtyard. A below-grade parking garage will include approximately 44 bike parking spaces and 19 vehicle parking spaces for residents and 9 curbside bike spaces for visitors.

Boston.name: 676 Washington Street
Boston.description: Proponent seeks to restore, renovate, expand and convert the long-existing Church Building at the Property Site into a multifamily residential development of up approximately 49,500 gross square feet, with up to 33 units of market rate and income restricted housing, below grade garaged parking and related site and access improvements at its newly sub-divided lot of approximately 38,968 square feet (the “Phase 1 Project”). It will retain a majority of the Church Building’s public facing front and side elevations along Washington Street, with a carefully designed and appropriately sited four (4) story addition at the rear.

Boston.name: 4259 - 4267 Washington Street
Boston.description: B’nai B’rith Housing (BBH), a regional nonprofit housing developer, proposes a new mixed-use, affordable senior housing development at 4259–4267 Washington Street in the Roslindale neighborhood of Boston. The project will create 41 units for seniors and older adults (age 55+), all of which will be affordable to households earning at or below 60% of Area Median Income (AMI). All units will contain one bedroom and one bathroom. The building will include a resident multi-purpose room, a fitness center, bike storage, management offices, shared laundry, a roof deck, and BBH’s resident service coordination. The ground floor will feature approximately 4,250 square feet of commercial space, which BBH intends to lease to the Thrift Shop of Boston, contingent upon the receipt of necessary funding from the City of Boston and the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. The site plan will include an outdoor courtyard space and improvements to the public realm along Washington Street.

Boston.name: 25 Supertest Street
Boston.description: 25 Supertest is a mixed use hotel / residential project with 130 keys and 108 residential units, and includes the development of Hood Green community open space.

Boston.name: 110 Wales Street
Boston.description: 40 ownership housing units with 34 indoor parking spaces.

Boston.name: 172 Western Avenue
Boston.description: The Proposed Project would consist of a new eight (8) story building with ground floor retail spaces. The street level will contain approximately 1,395 square feet of retail space and 1:1 bicycle parking following BPDA bicycle parking guidelines. One of the two proposed ground floor retail spaces will host the dry cleaners that has served the community since the 1960’s. Floors two through eight will contain twenty (20) total residential units, with a mix of twelve (12) one-bedroom units, seven (7) two-bedroom units, and one (1) three-bedroom unit. The Proposed Project will provide twenty (20) indoor long-term bicycle parking spaces and eight (8) outdoor short-term bicycle parking spaces across four (4) bike racks, for a total of twenty-eight (28) bicycle parking spaces. Trash and recycling will be serviced from Travis Street.

Boston.name: 150 Milk Street
Boston.description: The project involves the conversion of a partially occupied office building into a residential community, introducing approximately 18 new multifamily dwelling units across floors two through five. The ground floor will be reconfigured to include a residential lobby, associated amenities, and a mix of office and/or retail uses designed to activate the street level and contribute to the area’s evolving mixed-use fabric .

Boston.name: 4487 Washington Street
Boston.description: The proposed project located at 4487 Washington Street contemplates a new five-story residential building in Roslindale comprised of 28 dwelling units and 12 off-street parking spaces. The total lot area of the Project Site is approximately 11,058 square feet and the building will contain a total gross floor area of roughly 35,285 square feet.

Boston.name: 14-18 Hannon Street
Boston.description:
The Applicant proposes to construct a new 5-story residential building (the “New Building”) with a total of twenty-four (24) residential rental units (consisting of one-, two-, and three-
bedroom units), six (6) off-street parking spaces, and twenty-four (24) bicycle spaces on two parcels known and numbered as 14-18 Hannon Street (the “Proposed Project”). The New
Building will consist of approximately 23,520 gross square feet, and will feature a shared mail room and bike storage room on the ground floor as well as a roof deck.

Boston.name: 95 Berkeley Street

Two-thirds of these units will be two- and three-bedrooms to accommodate families. The project will be four stories and include 36 interior bike bike storage spots, eight exterior visitor bike parking spots, eight exterior vehicle parking spaces, and a community room with adjoining roof deck. Hollins Park draws inspiration from the surrounding Dorchester community and  will mesh with the neighborhood's architecture. The building will be fully accessible and residents will have elevator access to all floors, including the lobby, management office, community room, and residential units.

Resulting in a new net residential total of 202,000 sqft and approximately 255 new residential rental units. The proposed office-to-residential conversion presents an opportunity to reposition an underutilized downtown commercial building as a vibrant residential address, with ground floor retail, in the heart of Boston’s Financial District.

Boston.name: 50 Congress Street

Boston.name: 1200 Soldiers Field Road

Boston.name: 80 Christopher Street

Boston.name: 500 Gallivan Boulevard
Boston.description: The proposed project consists of new construction of a mixed-use building located at 500 Gallivan Boulevard in the Dorchester neighborhood of Boston. The site is currently occupied by a two-story structure formerly used as the Dorchester American Legion Post, which will be demolished to allow for redevelopment of the parcel. The project is intended to reinvest in an underutilized site along an established neighborhood corridor and contribute new residential and commercial activity consistent with the surrounding urban context. The proposed building will be five stories in height and will include ground-level commercial space with residential dwelling units located on the upper floors. A total of 24 residential units are proposed as part of the development, contributing to the City’s housing supply and supporting a mix of uses along Gallivan Boulevard. The design of the building and site will be evaluated through the Article 80 review process to ensure appropriate massing, access, and integration with adjacent uses and the public realm.  The building will have a total gross floor area of approximately 36,055 square feet and a maximum building height of approximately 58.5 feet. The project will provide 10 off-street parking spaces, along with associated access and site improvements, to support the proposed uses

Boston.name: One State Street
Boston.description: The Proponent seeks to renovate and convert approximately 64,428 gross square feet (“GSF”) of interior space within its existing 14-story commercial office building at the Project Site, by changing the legal use and occupancy from commercial office to residential multifamily housing of approximately 59,943 GSF on floors two (2) through fourteen (14) (the “Project”).   The Project includes an interior renovation and conversion only, with no expansion to the existing building’s footprint, GSF or exterior conditions.  Its existing ground floor commercial uses will also remain in place. As part of the City’s Downtown Office to Residential Conversion Pilot Program (the “Pilot Program”), the Project will create up to seventy-five (75) rental housing units, with up to 17% designated as income-restricted in compliance with the Pilot Program.    Details on the proposed Project, its site and architectural plans are included in this Application

Boston.name: 320 Summer Street
Boston.description: The proponent seeks to renovate, convert and expand the interior space within long-existing and combined brick and beam buildings at the site, by changing its legal use from commercial office to residential multifamily housing, with ground floor retail, and the construction of a partial mezzanine level to accommodate loft-style residential units. The project’s scope is limited to interior work within the combined buildings at the site, with no expansion to its existing footprint or façade. Specifically, and as part of the City’s Downtown Office to Residential Conversion Pilot Program (the “Pilot Program”), the project would create up  to 145 residential dwelling units in approximately 130,100 square feet of GFA, including ground floor retail of approximately 7,500 SF on A Street, approximately 2,398 SF of amenity space on its main level along Summer Street, and ample on-site bicycle storage. An existing roof deck of approximately 425 SF will be improved with accessibility accommodations for residential usage. Pursuant to the City’s Inclusionary Zoning requirements for its participation in the Pilot Program, the project would also create onsite income-restricted housing units.

Boston.name: 130 Dorchester Street
Boston.description: The project proposes the redevelopment of parcels known as and numbered 130 Dorchester Street in South Boston (the “Proposed Project”). The project proposes the conversion and rehabilitation of the former Marian Manor nursing home facility and other associated buildings to deliver approximately 204 residential rental apartment units with off-street parking for approximately 164 spaces. The development will be a joint venture between Beacon Communities LLC and the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association of New England, Inc. The streetscape along Essex Street will be enlivened via ground-floor commercial space, and the project also includes potential additional commercial support space in the basement.

Boston.name: 780 American Legion Highway
Boston.description:
The Property consists of approximately 2.58 acres located within the Roslindale neighborhood of Boston. It is currently occupied by the Home for Little Wanderers and contains existing office and community service uses, associated surface parking, circulation areas, and landscaped open space. The Property is mapped within the Two-Family Residential ("2F-5000 ") Subdistrict of the Roslindale Neighborhood District, as well as the Greenbelt Protection Overlay District (GPOD). While the applicable dimensional requirements and required permits will be further detailed in the forthcoming Project Notification Form, it is anticipated at this time that variances will be required for Use, Floor Area Ratio (FAR), Building Height, Usable Open Space, and Minimum Parking.

The Charles H. Farnsworth Housing Corporation is proposing the development of Farnsworth House II as a new, two-phase affordable senior housing community serving residents aged 62 and older. The current concept includes approximately 114 mixed-income affordable senior apartments across two buildings totaling approximately 140,000gsf. The unit mix is anticipated to consist primarily of one-bedroom apartments, with a limited number of two-bedroom units, including a manager’s unit.

The proposed development is intended to expand the availability of high-quality, affordable senior housing in Roslindale while incorporating supportive services and resident amenities that promote aging in community. The project is anticipated to include resident common areas, transportation services, a large multi-purpose room for resident and community programming, and an adult day health center that may serve both residents and the surrounding community.

Boston.name: 59 Meridian Street

The ground-floor commercial space will retain its long-standing retail tenant, Figaro’s sandwich shop, while repurposing unused ground-floor area into a residential lobby and additional commercial space. Totaling eight levels and approximately 343,630 SF, Alta XMBLY accommodates 329 residential units. Five levels of residential use sit above a three-story concrete podium. The podium supports retail, active uses and parking at the ground level, parking and back-of-house functions at level 2, and residential use at level 3. This building is consistent with the “Block Building” typology per the proposed Somerville Zoning Ordinance. Two lobbies support the activation of the ground level; the main lobby is located to serve as a “gateway” opportunity at the corner of Grand Union Boulevard and Revolution Drive, while the secondary lobby faces internal to the Site activating the corner of “Roads K and L”. A 2,700 SF retail/active space will anchor the corner of Grand Union Boulevard and “Road L”, a 4,489 SF retail space is provided on “Road K”, a 3,044 SF retail space is provided at the corner of “Road K” and Revolution Drive, and 412 SF bike room on Revolution Drive. Further activation along “Road K” (facing the central open space) is provided through the positioning of five (5) residential town house units with direct access to the sidewalk. The primary parking and loading entrances will be positioned along “Road L”. Parking will be provided at the ground level as well as Level 2 to support approximately 188 vehicles.

 Twenty-five (25) of these apartments will be rented to households with incomes at or below 50% of the Area Median Income (AMI), twenty-five (25) different apartments will be rented to households with incomes between 50% and 80% AMI, and sixteen (16) different apartments will be rent to households with incomes between 80% and 110% AMI.

Developer Armando Petruzziello is proposing a 24-unit condominium development at the site of the former Waban Health Center.  View the plans here. A special permit application was filed on August 26, 2019. Materials regarding the application are posted in the documents archive on this page. The new building would occupy generally the same footprint as the current building, except for some slight expansions (most notably along the north side facing Brae Burn). It would add a third floor and be 10 feet higher than the existing building for a total height of 34.5 feet. The units would be comprised of thirteen 1-bedroom units, nine 2-bedroom units, and two 3-bedroom units. As per Newton's current Inclusionary Zoning Ordinance, four of the units will be affordable (including one 3-bedroom unit).

The development would have 24 parking spots, all underground. The parking spots will be "unbundled" from the units, except that each of the affordable units will be assigned one parking spot. The underground parking garage would be accessed at the front NW corner of the building. The project would result in more greenspace than exists currently, due to elimination of the long driveway and outdoor parking area. The project will incorporate electric heat pumps and have solar panels on the roof, and the developer will seek to earn a LEED Silver rating.

The developer previously visited the Waban Area Council on May 9th to present his plans to the community and to solicit feedback.

Quincy.name: Quincy Center Train Station Development
Quincy.description:
The Quincy City Council gave its approval for the MBTA to enter into a development agreement with Atlantic Development and the Bozzuto Group. 

The Hingham-based Atlantic Development is partnering with the Bozzuto Group out of Washington, D.C., to propose to build on the 6.3-acre Quincy Center station land.

The two companies have proposed the Quincy Center development to happen in three phases, ideally starting in 2019 and finishing in 2031. The first stage would involve building 300 apartments plus some parking and a little commercial space on top of what’s now the parking lot in front of the station. That is unlikely to change dramatically.

The developers had proposed then to build another 300 apartments on top of the current station, but backed off that idea in the face of opposition from the council and other residents. Then final stage, to be completed around 2031, would be another 225,000 square feet of commercial use in the form of an office building suspended over the T tracks just south of the station.
